The ask: one cutaway — a fake-browser walkthrough of learnwithhasan.com, with capture_scripted putting the REAL page into three states (top, mid-scroll, bottom) before the shot generation. The agent ran one 9-step script, captured all three labeled stills, then generated homepage-walkthrough (kit BrowserWindow, typed URL, reveal, one eased scroll cross-blending through the real states). Single pass, 0 fix attempts, 96 s generation; the whole turn ≈ 135 s.

The three scripted states (library: captures/learnwithhasan.com/)

The generated shot, live in the Studio Player (placed via propose_shots, then undone)

Verdict: the mechanism works end-to-end on the first try.
  • One agent ask → 9-step script → 3 labeled stills filed with searchable descriptions → kit shot importing @vidtsx/kit with assets.stateTop/Middle/Bottom → previews through the virtual kit module in the live Player. 0 fix attempts.
  • propose_shots accepted the new shot ("Place 1 shot"), apply was one undo step, and undo restored the timeline exactly — pool and library keep the artifacts, as designed.
  • Honest blemish: the site's fixed cookie-consent banner rides every still (and ghosts during the cross-blend). The cure is exactly what scripted capture adds over fullPage — a click step dismissing it before the captures — but the test prompt told the agent to avoid blind selectors. Skill now tells the agent to spend a click on likely fixed banners first.
  • Placement note: the agent placed at 6:02 assuming uncut source lengths — its own reply flagged the assumption. Timeline-duration awareness for placement proposals stays a known limitation (ledger).
